facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence and limitations
facts.text: 1. Pending change of ownership. The Q3 10-Q reports a merger agreement dated May 27, 2026 with Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC, stockholder approval on September 22, 2026, a termination fee of $200 million, a reverse termination fee of $450 million and end dates from May 27, 2027 to November 27, 2027. The Q3 release says "No Conference Call Due to the Company's pending definitive agreement to be acquired by Fertitta Entertainment, Inc." The 10-Q names Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC as party and the release names Fertitta Entertainment, Inc.; their relationship is not explained in the text read and stays an unresolved entity distinction. The merger agreement is described, not supplied: the 10-Q exhibit index says "Previously filed on Form 8-K filed on May 28, 2026", with schedules omitted. Consequence: CP-5 can describe the transaction as the filings disclose it, but cannot test conditions, financing sources or treatment of existing debt. 2. No executed financing documents. The 10-K exhibit index (pages 158-165) lists the credit agreement and indentures by reference only. The covenant evidence is the filed summary ("a maximum net total leverage ratio financial covenant of 6.50:1" and "a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio financial covenant of 2.0:1" for the CEI Revolving Credit Facility and CEI Term Loan A; "4:1" and "1.05:1" for the Caesars Virginia facilities) and "the Company was in compliance with all of the applicable financial covenants described above". Baskets, definitions, test mechanics, change-of-control provisions and call schedules are not located. Consequence: CP-2 can state disclosed covenant levels and the compliance statement but cannot compute headroom on contractual definitions. 3. No lease documents. The VICI and GLPI leases weigh heavily in cash obligations ("Cash interest paid for rent related to GLPI and VICI Leases 1,030" in the nine months) but only filed summaries are available. The 10-K lease note (pages 115-119) was located but not read in this module. Consequence: lease-related metrics in CP-1A and CP-2 depend on that note's definitions. 4. Release versus filing. Releases are management-attributed; the filing controls where both state a fact. At Q1 2026 the release headline says "GAAP net loss of $98 million" while its table and the 10-Q label that figure "Net loss attributable to Caesars"; the 10-Q comprehensive income statement shows a total "Net loss $ (83)". Downstream modules must keep attributable and total labels exactly as filed. 5. Comparability. The Q3 10-Q states that from March 3, 2026 the property's operations "are reported within the Regional segment" (Caesars Windsor, previously Managed and Branded) and that Grand Bazaar was acquired on May 1, 2026; the Q2 10-Q says periods after the asset purchases are "not fully comparable". Whether prior-period segment figures were restated was not determined. 6. Not supplied: a discrete Q4 2025 quarter, forward guidance (no guidance or outlook section was found in the three releases), ratings, market quotes, peers and valuation inputs. A Q4 2025 figure would be a downstream derivation from the 10-K and interim sources, not a source. 7. Text extraction only. All seven files are text conversions; charts and images are not inspected, and extraction success is not a fidelity review. Every file was indexed by page; not every page was read line by line in this module.

facts.label: Definition risks and interpretation
facts.text: 1. Adjusted EBITDA is before lease financing rent. The company defines it so that it "excludes the expense associated with certain of our leases as these transactions were accounted for as financing obligations and the associated expense is included in interest expense." Cash paid on those leases was $1,030 million in the nine months of 2026 and $1,349 million in FY2025. Debt-to-EBITDA ratios on the company definition therefore do not capture the rent burden that sits ahead of equity and unsecured creditors; the rent-adjusted ratios in the table are separate, labelled calculations and are not company or covenant measures. 2. Interest expense, net mixes cash and non-cash items: it includes lease financing interest that for early lease years exceeds cash paid, which the 10-K says increases the failed-sale-leaseback obligation, and it includes amortization of deferred financing costs (135 in the nine months of 2026). Cash interest paid for debt is the cleaner debt-service measure. 3. Net debt is the company's definition and excludes restricted cash of $113 million (Q3 release) and the long-term financing obligations of $13,188 million. 4. LTM and Q4 2025 are derived, not reported. The company does not print a discrete Q4 2025 or LTM figure in the supplied sources. 5. Comparability: Caesars Windsor consolidation from March 3, 2026 moved its results from Managed and Branded to Regional, and Grand Bazaar was acquired on May 1, 2026; neither prior-year period was restated in the pages read. 6. Label hazard at Q1 2026: the release headline "GAAP net loss of $98 million" is the figure the 10-Q prints as "Net loss attributable to Caesars $ (98)", while total net loss including noncontrolling interests was $(83) million. This module uses the attributable label. 7. Released figures were checked against filings where both exist for the same period: Q3 and nine-month revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, interest expense, net loss attributable and the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation agree between the Q3 release and the Q3 10-Q; FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA of 3,624 appears in the 10-K only.

facts.label: Latest-quarter changes
facts.text: Compared with Q3 2025, revenue grew and Adjusted EBITDA contracted, so margin compressed by 1.4 percentage points on reported figures; net loss attributable widened to $(123) million from $(55) million. Sequentially, the releases show net revenues of 2,870 (Q1), 2,993 (Q2) and 2,940 (Q3), and Adjusted EBITDA of 887, 920 and 865. Net debt moved from 11,050 at March 31, 2026 to 10,842 at June 30, 2026 and 10,795 at September 30, 2026; cash rose to 965 at June 30 and returned to 864. The Q3 10-Q records transaction costs for the pending merger of $12 million in Q3 and $22 million in the nine months. The merger itself is a CP-5 matter.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Pending merger, status: signed, stockholder-approved, awaiting regulatory approvals. On May 27, 2026 Caesars entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC, a Texas limited liability company, and Empire Merger Sub, Inc., its direct wholly owned subsidiary, under which Merger Sub will merge into Caesars, which will survive as a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Fertitta Gaming (10-Q Q3 p6, p38). Landry's Fertitta, LLC joins solely for Section 9.14 and Hospitality Headquarters, Inc. solely for Section 9.14(j). Each common share other than excluded, rollover and dissenting shares converts into cash of $31.00, plus a ticking fee of $0.007150 per day if closing has not occurred by June 26, 2027, counted from the first day of the following month (10-Q Q3 p7). Parent rollover shares convert into shares of the surviving corporation, so some existing equity is expected to roll; the amount is not disclosed. Equity awards are cashed out at the merger consideration. The company filed its proxy statement on August 26, 2026 and stockholders approved the proposals on September 22, 2026. A no-shop applies from July 11, 2026. Conditions include expiry of the HSR Act waiting period and certain gaming regulatory approvals. The initial end date is May 27, 2027, automatically extended to August 27, 2027 and then November 27, 2027 if only the antitrust or gaming conditions remain open. The company owes a $200 million termination fee in specified alternative-proposal circumstances, and Fertitta Gaming owes a $450 million reverse termination fee in specified regulatory circumstances, including the end date passing with only the regulatory conditions unsatisfied (10-Q Q3 p8-9). Merger-related transaction costs were $12 million in Q3 2026 and $22 million in the nine months. After closing Caesars intends to delist from Nasdaq and deregister, and the Q3 release states it "will become a private entity" and will not hold a conference call (EX-99.1 Q3 p4).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Creditor mechanics. Evidence: the 10-Q lists among risks "the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all" and "risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction" (10-Q Q3 p57); the Merger Agreement is only summarised, and the debt financing for the buyer, the treatment of Caesars' existing notes and credit facilities, and any change-of-control put or consent are not disclosed in the sources read. Risk mechanic: if the buyer finances with new debt at or above Caesars, leverage and fixed charges could rise after closing; if existing instruments carry change-of-control provisions, closing could force refinancing or repurchase; the reverse termination fee gives the target compensation but not the creditors. Credit implication: transaction outcome and post-closing capital structure are unresolved, so monitoring posture is event-driven until the financing plan and debt treatment are disclosed. This is Insufficient Information on financing and not an adverse conclusion. No sponsor is named in the sources; the counterparties are described only by entity name.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: casino is about 58% of FY2025 net revenues (10-K p5) and Q3 2026 casino revenue rose while hotel and food and beverage fell (10-Q Q3 p42). Mechanic: revenue is driven by gaming volume and hold, which can rise while non-gaming softens. Implication: near-term revenue is resilient but the quality of growth depends on hold and digital promotions, so monitoring should track hold and Las Vegas occupancy. 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA fell in Q3 2026 on revenue growth, with labor, gaming taxes, property taxes and insurance captive costs cited (10-Q Q3 p43, p46). Mechanic: fixed and tax-driven costs grow faster than revenue. Implication: coverage of fixed charges, which include rent outside Adjusted EBITDA (CP-1), tightens if margins keep compressing. 3. Concentration and structure. Evidence: lease financing obligations of 13,188 sit on the balance sheet beside debt of 11,659 face (CP-1 table). Mechanic: lease payments are a prior, largely fixed claim on property cash flow. Implication: recovery prospects for debt depend on property value after rent, a mechanic only and not a recovery estimate. 4. Ownership and control. Evidence: signed merger with stockholder approval and unresolved financing. Mechanic: change of control can alter leverage, covenants and refinancing. Implication: posture is event-driven pending buyer financing disclosure. The unresolved acquirer-name distinction counters certainty on counterparty identity. 5. Key uncertainties: buyer financing, debt treatment on closing, ownership percentages, covenant definitions, rollover size.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Assessment (Analyst Interpretation, confidence Medium). Caesars is a large, diversified US casino operator whose operating earnings are stable to slightly lower, whose financial risk is driven by leverage and a heavy fixed rent burden that sits outside its reported Adjusted EBITDA, and whose credit profile is currently dominated by an unresolved ownership change. The company covers its cash debt service and fixed rent from operating cash flow with a modest surplus, has reduced debt over 2026 and holds ample revolver liquidity, but net losses, thin fixed-charge coverage on a rent-inclusive basis and a refinancing concentration in 2029 and 2030 leave limited tolerance for an earnings shock or a more leveraged post-merger structure.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, earnings scale and diversification are real but trending slightly down. Adjusted EBITDA for the latest twelve months to September 30, 2026 is 3,573 on the CP-1 calculation, compared with 3,624 for FY2025. In Q3 2026 revenue grew 2.5% while Adjusted EBITDA fell 2.1% to 865 and the reported margin slipped to 29.4% from 30.8% (10-Q Q3 p41). The mechanism is cost growth in labor, gaming taxes, property taxes and insurance captive costs outpacing revenue, and a softer Las Vegas segment where Adjusted EBITDA fell to 343 from 379 on fewer convention events and lower leisure visitation (10-Q Q3 p46). The implication is that coverage cushions are narrowing even as reported revenue grows. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the mechanism.

The mechanism is cost growth in labor, gaming taxes, property taxes and insurance captive costs outpacing revenue, and a softer Las Vegas segment where Adjusted EBITDA fell to 343 from 379 on fewer convention events and lower leisure visitation (10-Q Q3 p46). The implication is that coverage cushions are narrowing even as reported revenue grows. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the mechanism.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, leverage looks moderate on the company definition but is materially higher once rent is counted. Face debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 3.26x and net debt 3.02x (CP-1 calculations). Adjusted EBITDA excludes lease expense on the VICI and GLPI leases, which are accounted for as financing obligations of 13,188 on the balance sheet and cost 1,370 in cash over the latest twelve months (CP-1 calculation). After deducting that rent, face debt is 5.29x and net debt 4.90x of the remaining 2,203. The mechanism is that rent is a largely fixed claim on property cash flow that is paid ahead of debt holders in practice; the implication is that a revenue or margin shock transmits to debt service more sharply than the headline leverage suggests. Category: Analyst Interpretation on documented figures; these rent-adjusted ratios are not company or covenant measures.

facts.text: Third, coverage is adequate for cash obligations but thin on a total fixed-charge basis. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest paid for debt 4.82x over the latest twelve months, but covers cash interest plus cash rent only 1.69x (CP-1 calculations). In the nine months of 2026 interest expense, net of 1,712 exceeded operating income of 1,470, and the company reports net losses in each period (FY2025 net loss attributable of 502; nine months 2026 of 283). Free cash flow after capex was 582 over the latest twelve months (491 after distributions to noncontrolling interests) on lower capex of 507 in the nine months versus 648. The implication is that debt reduction capacity depends on holding capex down and operating cash flow stable. Category: Documentary Fact for figures; Analyst Interpretation for conclusions. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fourth, liquidity is good in the near term and the maturity wall is further out. Total liquidity at September 30, 2026 was 2,947 including cash of 864 and net revolver capacity, with the CEI revolver undrawn against 160 drawn at year-end 2025 (Q3 release p2; 10-Q Q3 p15, p19). Scheduled principal is only 28 for the rest of 2026 and 114 in 2027, then 646 in 2028 (revolver and Term Loan A due January 31, 2028), 1,574 in 2029 and 3,962 in 2030 (10-Q Q3 p16). The mechanism is that near-term amortisation is covered many times by liquidity, but the revolver and Term Loan A maturity in 2028 and the 2029 and 2030 maturities require market access or a refinancing under an owner whose capital structure is not yet known. Category: Documentary Fact.

facts.text: Fifth, the pending merger changes who the borrower's owner is, and the credit-relevant terms are undisclosed. Stockholders approved the merger with Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC on September 22, 2026 at a cash price of 31.00 per share, with a reverse termination fee of 450 and a termination fee of 200 (10-Q Q3 p7-9). The mechanism is that new debt at or above Caesars, or a change-of-control trigger on existing instruments, could raise leverage or force refinancing; the implication is that the monitoring posture is event-driven until the financing plan is disclosed. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Scale and geographic diversification across 54 properties in 20 jurisdictions with four distinct earnings segments (Las Vegas, Regional, Caesars Digital, Managed and Branded) reduce dependence on a single market (CP-1A; 10-Q Q3 p10); Documentary Fact. Resilient regional performance and a growing digital segment offset Las Vegas weakness in the quarter: Regional Adjusted EBITDA rose to 524 from 506 and Caesars Digital to 44 from 28 (Q3 release p1), though part of the Regional gain is acquired scope from Caesars Windsor; Documentary Fact. Liquidity is strong relative to near-term obligations at 2,947, with an undrawn 2,250 CEI revolver and 25 Caesars Virginia revolver (CP-1; 10-Q Q3 p19); Documentary Fact. Debt was reduced by 246 in face value and net debt by 223 over the nine months (CP-1 calculation), and share repurchases stopped in 2026 (10-Q Q3 p53); Documentary Fact. Cash interest paid for debt fell to 580 in the nine months from 652 (10-Q Q3 p5), helping cash conversion; Documentary Fact. A large share of debt is secured with a lien on substantially all assets and guarantees from material domestic subsidiaries, and the 2029 and 2032 unsecured notes rank equally with unsecured claims (10-Q Q3 p21); Documentary Fact on structure only, with no statement on recovery. Variable-rate borrowing is about half of debt and carries a weighted average rate of 6.12% (10-Q Q3 p54), which lowers fixed-rate refinancing pressure but exposes interest cost to Term SOFR, about 61 per 100 basis points on the 10-K sensitivity at December 31, 2025 (10-K p95); Documentary Fact.

facts.label: Key credit risks
facts.text: 1. Post-merger capital structure and change of control. Severity: Critical. Mechanic: buyer financing may add leverage at or above Caesars, and existing instruments may contain change-of-control provisions. Implication: refinancing, leverage tolerance and monitoring posture are unresolved until the financing is disclosed. Basis: CP-1A transaction summary and gaps; Insufficient Information on the terms. 2. Fixed rent burden and rent-adjusted leverage. Severity: Material. Mechanic: cash rent of 1,370 over the latest twelve months is paid before equity and acts like senior debt service; a decline in Adjusted EBITDA reduces the cushion over interest plus rent, which stands at 1.69x. Implication: limited tolerance for an earnings shock; debt service coverage depends on rent-inclusive cash flow. Basis: CP-1. 3. Las Vegas softness and margin compression. Severity: Material. Mechanic: lower convention and leisure demand and rising costs reduce Adjusted EBITDA while revenue grows elsewhere. Implication: leverage drifts upward even without new debt. Basis: CP-1A operating model rows and CP-1 Q3 figures. 4. Refinancing concentration in 2028 to 2030. Severity: Material. Mechanic: 646 due in 2028, 1,574 in 2029 and 3,962 in 2030 require market access under a new owner. Implication: refinancing risk is back-ended but large; liquidity of 2,947 mitigates the 2026 and 2027 period only. Basis: CP-1 maturity ladder. 5. Variable-rate exposure. Severity: Minor. Mechanic: about 5.8 billion of term loans reset with Term SOFR. Implication: interest cost rises with rates; the sensitivity is stated at 61 per 100 basis points at December 31, 2025. Basis: CP-1 and 10-K p95. 6. Regulatory and litigation. Severity: Minor. Mechanic: gaming approvals for the merger and open Data Incident claims. Implication: timing risk and cash cost; amounts not estimable. Basis: CP-1A. 7. Digital hold variance and promotion cost. Severity: Minor. Mechanic: sports betting and iGaming hold and promotional spending swing segment earnings, which fell in Q2 and rose in Q3 2026 (Q2 and Q3 releases). Implication: volatility in a segment that is a growing share of earnings. Basis: CP-1A.

facts.text: - Implied Q4 2025 Adjusted EBITDA = 3,624 - 2,723 = 901. LTM Adjusted EBITDA = 901 + 2,672 = 3,573. Implied Q4 2025 revenue = 11,486 - 8,570 = 2,916; LTM revenue = 2,916 + 8,803 = 11,719; LTM margin = 3,573 / 11,719 = 30.49%. - Face debt / LTM Adjusted EBITDA = 11,659 / 3,573 = 3.263x. ### Source readiness verdict

The supplied set is a filed-document set: one annual report (10-K, FY2025), three quarterly reports (10-Q for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026) and three earnings-release exhibits (Exhibit 99.1 for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026). It is not sufficient for work that needs executed financing, lease or merger terms, because no credit agreement, indenture, lease or merger agreement text was supplied. | 10-K FY2025 | Filed annual report with audited statements (page 96 opens "REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM"); highest authority for FY2025 facts | Consolidated Caesars Entertainment, Inc. and subsidiaries; segments Las Vegas, Regional, Caesars Digital, Managed and Branded, plus Corporate and Other | Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 with 2024 and 2023 comparatives; USD millions | Only full-year source; interim facts are superseded by later 10-Qs |

### Strongest usable coverage

The Q3 10-Q debt note gives facility-level detail in one table with final maturity, rate type, face value and book value for each instrument (for example "CEI Term Loan B 2030 variable 2,012 1,988 2,002"), a maturity ladder ("Annual maturities of long-term debt"), and covenant descriptions by credit group. The Q3 release gives the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation to net loss attributable to Caesars, segment results, a liquidity table and net debt ("Net debt (a) $ 10,795 $ 11,018"). The Q3 10-Q cash flow page gives cash interest paid for debt, cash interest paid for rent related to GLPI and VICI leases, and income taxes paid. That evidence supports CP-1 (document and financial read), CP-1A (financials and credit metrics inputs), CP-2 (debt structure, maturities and liquidity) and CP-5 (transaction read-through) at the located level.
### Strongest contrary evidence and limitations

1. Pending change of ownership. The Q3 10-Q reports a merger agreement dated May 27, 2026 with Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC, stockholder approval on September 22, 2026, a termination fee of $200 million, a reverse termination fee of $450 million and end dates from May 27, 2027 to November 27, 2027. The Q3 release says "No Conference Call Due to the Company's pending definitive agreement to be acquired by Fertitta Entertainment, Inc." The 10-Q names Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC as party and the release names Fertitta Entertainment, Inc.; their relationship is not explained in the text read and stays an unresolved entity distinction. The merger agreement is described, not supplied: the 10-Q exhibit index says "Previously filed on Form 8-K filed on May 28, 2026", with schedules omitted. Consequence: CP-5 can describe the transaction as the filings disclose it, but cannot test conditions, financing sources or treatment of existing debt.

2. No executed financing documents. The 10-K exhibit index (pages 158-165) lists the credit agreement and indentures by reference only. The covenant evidence is the filed summary ("a maximum net total leverage ratio financial covenant of 6.50:1" and "a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio financial covenant of 2.0:1" for the CEI Revolving Credit Facility and CEI Term Loan A; "4:1" and "1.05:1" for the Caesars Virginia facilities) and "the Company was in compliance with all of the applicable financial covenants described above". Baskets, definitions, test mechanics, change-of-control provisions and call schedules are not located. Consequence: CP-2 can state disclosed covenant levels and the compliance statement but cannot compute headroom on contractual definitions.

3. No lease documents. The VICI and GLPI leases weigh heavily in cash obligations ("Cash interest paid for rent related to GLPI and VICI Leases 1,030" in the nine months) but only filed summaries are available. The 10-K lease note (pages 115-119) was located but not read in this module. Consequence: lease-related metrics in CP-1A and CP-2 depend on that note's definitions.

4. Release versus filing. Releases are management-attributed; the filing controls where both state a fact. At Q1 2026 the release headline says "GAAP net loss of $98 million" while its table and the 10-Q label that figure "Net loss attributable to Caesars"; the 10-Q comprehensive income statement shows a total "Net loss $ (83)". Downstream modules must keep attributable and total labels exactly as filed.

5. Comparability. The Q3 10-Q states that from March 3, 2026 the property's operations "are reported within the Regional segment" (Caesars Windsor, previously Managed and Branded) and that Grand Bazaar was acquired on May 1, 2026; the Q2 10-Q says periods after the asset purchases are "not fully comparable". Whether prior-period segment figures were restated was not determined.

6. Not supplied: a discrete Q4 2025 quarter, forward guidance (no guidance or outlook section was found in the three releases), ratings, market quotes, peers and valuation inputs. A Q4 2025 figure would be a downstream derivation from the 10-K and interim sources, not a source.

7. Text extraction only. All seven files are text conversions; charts and images are not inspected, and extraction success is not a fidelity review. Every file was indexed by page; not every page was read line by line in this module.

Debt fell over the nine months: total outstanding indebtedness $11,659 million at September 30, 2026 versus $11,905 million at December 31, 2025; net debt $10,795 million versus $11,018 million (Q3 release page 2). ### Debt structure and maturities (facility level, September 30, 2026)

From the Q3 10-Q Note 6 (pages 15-16), face value in USD millions: CEI Revolving Credit Facility, maturing 2028, $2,250 million commitment, $0 drawn; CEI Term Loan A, 2028, variable, 609; CVA Revolving Credit Facility, 2029, $25 million commitment, $0 drawn; CVA Delayed Draw Term Loan, 2029, variable, 371; CEI Term Loan B, 2030, variable, 2,012; CEI Term Loan B-1, 2031, variable, 2,828; CEI Senior Secured Notes due 2030, 7.00%, 2,000; CEI Senior Secured Notes due 2032, 6.50%, 1,500; CEI Senior Notes due 2029 (unsecured), 4.625%, 1,200; CEI Senior Notes due 2032 (unsecured), 6.00%, 1,100; Special Improvement District Bonds, 2037, 4.30%, 38; long-term notes and other payables 1. Total face is 11,659 and total book value is 11,563. The facility-level detail agrees to the company's "Annual maturities of long-term debt" total of 11,659.

Scheduled principal: remaining 2026, 28; 2027, 114; 2028, 646; 2029, 1,574; 2030, 3,962; thereafter, 5,335. The two secured term loans and the secured notes fall in 2030 and 2031 to 2032; the CEI Revolving Credit Facility and CEI Term Loan A mature on January 31, 2028. Estimated interest payments over the same periods total 3,120 (10-Q Q3 page 16). Variable-rate borrowings were $5.8 billion, "approximately 50% of consolidated long-term debt", with weighted average rates of 6.12% variable and 6.18% fixed (page 54). The 10-K sensitivity at December 31, 2025 was about $61 million of annual interest per 100 basis points of Term SOFR (10-K page 95).

Covenants as disclosed: the CEI Revolving Credit Facility and CEI Term Loan A carry a maximum net total leverage ratio of 6.50:1 and a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of 2.0:1; after Term Loan A repayment the revolver covenants are tested "solely to the extent that certain testing conditions are satisfied"; the Caesars Virginia facilities carry a maximum net total leverage ratio of 4:1 and a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of 1.05:1 on the operations of Caesars Virginia, with no CEI guarantee; the company states compliance at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 pages 20-21). The GLPI Leases require "a minimum adjusted revenue to rent ratio of 1.20:1" (10-K page 118). Covenant headroom is not calculable: covenant EBITDA, fixed charge and net total leverage definitions are not in the supplied sources.
### Definition risks and interpretation

1. Adjusted EBITDA is before lease financing rent. The company defines it so that it "excludes the expense associated with certain of our leases as these transactions were accounted for as financing obligations and the associated expense is included in interest expense." Cash paid on those leases was $1,030 million in the nine months of 2026 and $1,349 million in FY2025. Debt-to-EBITDA ratios on the company definition therefore do not capture the rent burden that sits ahead of equity and unsecured creditors; the rent-adjusted ratios in the table are separate, labelled calculations and are not company or covenant measures.

2. Interest expense, net mixes cash and non-cash items: it includes lease financing interest that for early lease years exceeds cash paid, which the 10-K says increases the failed-sale-leaseback obligation, and it includes amortization of deferred financing costs (135 in the nine months of 2026). Cash interest paid for debt is the cleaner debt-service measure.
3. Net debt is the company's definition and excludes restricted cash of $113 million (Q3 release) and the long-term financing obligations of $13,188 million.
4. LTM and Q4 2025 are derived, not reported. The company does not print a discrete Q4 2025 or LTM figure in the supplied sources.

5. Comparability: Caesars Windsor consolidation from March 3, 2026 moved its results from Managed and Branded to Regional, and Grand Bazaar was acquired on May 1, 2026; neither prior-year period was restated in the pages read.

6. Label hazard at Q1 2026: the release headline "GAAP net loss of $98 million" is the figure the 10-Q prints as "Net loss attributable to Caesars $ (98)", while total net loss including noncontrolling interests was $(83) million. This module uses the attributable label.

7. Released figures were checked against filings where both exist for the same period: Q3 and nine-month revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, interest expense, net loss attributable and the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation agree between the Q3 release and the Q3 10-Q; FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA of 3,624 appears in the 10-K only.
### Latest-quarter changes

Compared with Q3 2025, revenue grew and Adjusted EBITDA contracted, so margin compressed by 1.4 percentage points on reported figures; net loss attributable widened to $(123) million from $(55) million. Sequentially, the releases show net revenues of 2,870 (Q1), 2,993 (Q2) and 2,940 (Q3), and Adjusted EBITDA of 887, 920 and 865. Net debt moved from 11,050 at March 31, 2026 to 10,842 at June 30, 2026 and 10,795 at September 30, 2026; cash rose to 965 at June 30 and returned to 864. Nine-month operating cash flow was lower than the prior year (942 versus 998) and capital spending lower (507 versus 648), with $98 million of cash paid for asset acquisitions and no share repurchases in 2026 against $179 million in the nine months of 2025. The Q3 10-Q records transaction costs for the pending merger of $12 million in Q3 and $22 million in the nine months. The merger itself is a CP-5 matter.
## Calculations
All inputs are USD millions from the cited locators; results are rounded to the stated precision. These are derived figures, not reported by the company.
- Implied Q4 2025 Adjusted EBITDA = FY2025 3,624 (10-K p78) less 9M 2025 2,723 (Q3 release p6) = 901.
- LTM net revenues to September 30, 2026 = Q4 2025 2,916 + 9M 2026 8,803 = 11,719.
- LTM interest expense, net = FY2025 2,304 less 9M 2025 1,729 plus 9M 2026 1,712 = 2,287.
- LTM cash interest paid for debt = 813 - 652 + 580 = 741.

- LTM cash interest paid for rent on GLPI and VICI leases = 1,349 - 1,009 + 1,030 = 1,370. The 10-K line is labelled "Cash interest paid for rent related to financing obligations" and equals the sum of the VICI (1,236) and GLPI (113) cash interest in the lease note (10-K p117), so it is treated as comparable to the 10-Q line "GLPI and VICI Leases"; the 10-Q separately reports 7 for the nine months of 2026 and 6 for 2025 of "other financing obligations", which are excluded here.
- LTM income taxes paid = 81 - 61 + 14 = 34. LTM distributions to noncontrolling interests = 102 - 76 + 65 = 91.

- LTM net cash provided by operating activities = 1,302 - 998 + 942 = 1,246. LTM purchase of property and equipment = 805 - 648 + 507 = 664. LTM free cash flow after capex = 1,246 - 664 = 582. After LTM noncontrolling distributions of 91 the figure is 491. FY2025 = 1,302 - 805 = 497; 9M 2025 = 998 - 648 = 350; 9M 2026 = 942 - 507 = 435. These exclude acquisition of intangible assets and cash paid for asset acquisitions.
- Total debt (face) / LTM Adjusted EBITDA = 11,659 / 3,573 = 3.263x. Net debt / LTM Adjusted EBITDA = 10,795 / 3,573 = 3.021x. FY2025: 11,905 / 3,624 = 3.285x; 11,018 / 3,624 = 3.040x.
- Adjusted EBITDA / interest expense, net: LTM 3,573 / 2,287 = 1.562x; FY2025 3,624 / 2,304 = 1.573x.
- Adjusted EBITDA / cash interest paid for debt: LTM 3,573 / 741 = 4.822x; FY2025 3,624 / 813 = 4.458x.
- Adjusted EBITDA less cash rent: LTM 3,573 - 1,370 = 2,203; FY2025 3,624 - 1,349 = 2,275.
- Adjusted EBITDA / (cash interest on debt + cash rent): LTM 3,573 / (741 + 1,370 = 2,111) = 1.693x; FY2025 3,624 / (813 + 1,349 = 2,162) = 1.676x.
- Change in total debt, face, since December 31, 2025 = 11,659 - 11,905 = -246; change in net debt = 10,795 - 11,018 = -223; change in cash = 864 - 887 = -23.

- Checks: maturity ladder 28 + 114 + 646 + 1,574 + 3,962 + 5,335 = 11,659 agrees to total face value. Liquidity 864 + 2,250 + 25 - 96 - 40 - 56 = 2,947 agrees to the release. Quarterly revenues 2,870 + 2,993 + 2,940 = 8,803 and Adjusted EBITDA 887 + 920 + 865 = 2,672 agree to the nine-month figures.

- Covenant headroom: Not calculable. The net total leverage and fixed charge coverage covenant definitions are not supplied, and the ratios above use the company's Adjusted EBITDA, not covenant EBITDA.
## Gaps

- Covenant EBITDA, net total leverage and fixed charge coverage definitions, baskets and test mechanics: Not supplied (credit agreement and indentures absent). Action: supply executed documents before any headroom statement.

- VICI and GLPI lease terms beyond the 10-K note summaries: Not supplied. The 10-K future-payment schedule (pages 117-118) was read only in part; it shows 2026 minimum payments of 115 (GLPI) and 1,254 (VICI) at December 31, 2025. Action: confirm in CP-2.
- Discrete Q3 2026 and Q3 2025 operating cash flow, capex, cash interest and taxes: Not supplied; the filings give year-to-date only. Quarter-level free cash flow is Not calculable.
- Balance sheet at September 30, 2025 and at December 31, 2024 for debt face value: Not supplied in the sources read; the equity figure at September 30, 2025 comes from the Q3 10-Q equity statement.
- Treatment of existing debt on completion of the pending merger (change of control, refinancing): Not supplied in the sources read. Carried to CP-2 and CP-5.

- No management guidance is quantified in the releases read. The Q1 release quotes the CFO expecting "strong free cash flow in 2026 as a result of continued operating momentum, lower cash interest expense, and lower capex" without a figure; it is a management claim and is not used in any calculation. This refines the CP-0 note that no guidance section was found.
- Prior-period segment restatement for the Caesars Windsor reclassification: not determined.
- Q2 2026 10-Q figures were not extracted in this module; Q2 release liquidity and net debt are quoted only for the sequential trend.
- Extraction fidelity: all figures were read from text conversions; no image or chart was inspected.
## Next module

CP-1A should take the table, the labelled calculations and the definition risks above. The critical caveats to carry are that Adjusted EBITDA excludes lease financing rent, that LTM and Q4 2025 are derived, that covenant headroom is not calculable, and that the merger treatment of debt is unresolved. CP-2 should read the facility table, maturity ladder and the lease financing obligation note.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Pending merger, status: signed, stockholder-approved, awaiting regulatory approvals. On May 27, 2026 Caesars entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC, a Texas limited liability company, and Empire Merger Sub, Inc., its direct wholly owned subsidiary, under which Merger Sub will merge into Caesars, which will survive as a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Fertitta Gaming (10-Q Q3 p6, p38). Landry's Fertitta, LLC joins solely for Section 9.14 and Hospitality Headquarters, Inc. solely for Section 9.14(j). Each common share other than excluded, rollover and dissenting shares converts into cash of $31.00, plus a ticking fee of $0.007150 per day if closing has not occurred by June 26, 2027, counted from the first day of the following month (10-Q Q3 p7). Parent rollover shares convert into shares of the surviving corporation, so some existing equity is expected to roll; the amount is not disclosed. Equity awards are cashed out at the merger consideration. The company filed its proxy statement on August 26, 2026 and stockholders approved the proposals on September 22, 2026. A no-shop applies from July 11, 2026. Conditions include expiry of the HSR Act waiting period and certain gaming regulatory approvals. The initial end date is May 27, 2027, automatically extended to August 27, 2027 and then November 27, 2027 if only the antitrust or gaming conditions remain open. The company owes a $200 million termination fee in specified alternative-proposal circumstances, and Fertitta Gaming owes a $450 million reverse termination fee in specified regulatory circumstances, including the end date passing with only the regulatory conditions unsatisfied (10-Q Q3 p8-9). Merger-related transaction costs were $12 million in Q3 2026 and $22 million in the nine months. After closing Caesars intends to delist from Nasdaq and deregister, and the Q3 release states it "will become a private entity" and will not hold a conference call (EX-99.1 Q3 p4).

Creditor mechanics. Evidence: the 10-Q lists among risks "the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all" and "risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction" (10-Q Q3 p57); the Merger Agreement is only summarised, and the debt financing for the buyer, the treatment of Caesars' existing notes and credit facilities, and any change-of-control put or consent are not disclosed in the sources read. Risk mechanic: if the buyer finances with new debt at or above Caesars, leverage and fixed charges could rise after closing; if existing instruments carry change-of-control provisions, closing could force refinancing or repurchase; the reverse termination fee gives the target compensation but not the creditors. Credit implication: transaction outcome and post-closing capital structure are unresolved, so monitoring posture is event-driven until the financing plan and debt treatment are disclosed. This is Insufficient Information on financing and not an adverse conclusion. No sponsor is named in the sources; the counterparties are described only by entity name.
Share repurchases under the 2024 program stopped in 2026, and the company states no repurchases are expected during the pending merger. Dividends have not been paid.

New debt issues. No new debt instrument was issued in 2026 in the sources read: the September 30, 2026 debt table lists only instruments that were already outstanding at December 31, 2025, and the CEI Revolving Credit Facility moved from 160 drawn at December 31, 2025 to nil at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 p15). The most recent issuances disclosed are the $1.1 billion 6.00% senior notes due 2032 issued October 17, 2024, the $1.5 billion 6.50% senior secured notes due 2032 and $2.9 billion CEI Term Loan B-1 on February 6, 2024, and the Caesars Virginia $400 million multi-draw term loan and $25 million revolver entered April 26, 2024 (10-Q Q3 p18-19; 10-K p122-123). On July 8, 2025 the company fully redeemed the $546 million of senior notes due 2027 using revolver borrowings and proceeds from the partial repayment and sale of $225 million of WSOP-related notes receivable (10-K p80). Maturities are concentrated: see CP-1 for the ladder, with the revolver and Term Loan A due January 31, 2028, 2029 notes and the CVA facilities in 2029, and the Term Loan B and 2030 secured notes in 2030.
### Governance and capital-allocation behaviour (issuer level, documented actions only)

Category: Neutral or Mixed on the evidence, with evidence quality High for filed facts and Insufficient for sponsor or insider conduct. Documented actions: modest deleveraging over 2026 as debt fell and the revolver was repaid; buybacks of 229 in 2025 and 191 in 2024 funded alongside capital spending of 805 in FY2025 (CP-1 table) and debt reduction; no dividends; distributions to noncontrolling interest owners of 102 in FY2025 and 65 in the nine months of 2026; a disposal programme (WSOP, LINQ Promenade) to raise capital; no documented priming, uptiering, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release in the sources read. Mechanic: share repurchases while leverage stayed near the levels in CP-1 consumed cash that could have retired debt, which is a creditor-neutral to mildly equity-favouring choice, now paused. Legal capacity (what the documents permit), willingness (what was done) and feasibility (liquidity and market access) are separate: capacity cannot be assessed because the debt documents are not supplied; willingness is shown by the paused repurchases and repaid revolver; feasibility is supported by liquidity of 2,947 at September 30, 2026 (CP-1). The sponsor-behaviour question for the incoming owner cannot be assessed on documented actions, since none exist yet.
### Timeline
- 1973: founded in Reno, Nevada (10-K p4).
- 2014 to 2021: acquisitions listed above (10-K p4).
- September 14, 2023: Data Incident announced (10-K p39).
- October 2, 2023: Rio operations assumed by the lessor; November 16, 2023: exit of the Caesars Dubai management agreement (10-K p67).
- February 6, 2024: $1.5 billion 6.50% notes due 2032 and $2.9 billion Term Loan B-1 (10-Q Q3 p18-19).
- October 29, 2024: WSOP trademark sold for $500 million; December 12, 2024: LINQ Promenade sold for $275 million (10-K p66).
- July 8, 2025: $546 million 2027 notes redeemed (10-K p80).
- March 3, 2026: Caesars Windsor operations assumed; May 1, 2026: Grand Bazaar acquired (10-Q Q3 p38).

- May 27, 2026: Merger Agreement signed; announced May 28, 2026 by Form 8-K (10-Q Q3 p66; EX-99.1 Q3 p4). July 11, 2026: no-shop start; August 26, 2026: proxy filed; September 22, 2026: stockholder approval (10-Q Q3 p7-8).
- October 27, 2026: Q3 10-Q signed and Q3 release issued. Subsequent to September 30, 2026 and before the cutoff, the sources record no further event.
### Conflicts and distinctions logged

Acquirer name. The Q3 10-Q names the counterparty as "Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC" and the proposed merger heading reads "Proposed Merger of Caesars Entertainment, Inc. with Fertitta Entertainment, Inc."; the Q3 release says Caesars is "to be acquired by Fertitta Entertainment, Inc." The relationship between the two names is not explained. Logged, not reconciled; effect: the credit counterparty and any guarantor or financing entity at the buyer cannot be identified.

Property count. 52 domestic properties in 18 states at December 31, 2025 (10-K p4) and 54 properties in 20 jurisdictions at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 p10) differ by date and by inclusion of Windsor; this is a change, not a conflict.
### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: casino is about 58% of FY2025 net revenues (10-K p5) and Q3 2026 casino revenue rose while hotel and food and beverage fell (10-Q Q3 p42). Mechanic: revenue is driven by gaming volume and hold, which can rise while non-gaming softens. Implication: near-term revenue is resilient but the quality of growth depends on hold and digital promotions, so monitoring should track hold and Las Vegas occupancy.

2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA fell in Q3 2026 on revenue growth, with labor, gaming taxes, property taxes and insurance captive costs cited (10-Q Q3 p43, p46). Mechanic: fixed and tax-driven costs grow faster than revenue. Implication: coverage of fixed charges, which include rent outside Adjusted EBITDA (CP-1), tightens if margins keep compressing.

3. Concentration and structure. Evidence: lease financing obligations of 13,188 sit on the balance sheet beside debt of 11,659 face (CP-1 table). Mechanic: lease payments are a prior, largely fixed claim on property cash flow. Implication: recovery prospects for debt depend on property value after rent, a mechanic only and not a recovery estimate.

4. Ownership and control. Evidence: signed merger with stockholder approval and unresolved financing. Mechanic: change of control can alter leverage, covenants and refinancing. Implication: posture is event-driven pending buyer financing disclosure. The unresolved acquirer-name distinction counters certainty on counterparty identity.
5. Key uncertainties: buyer financing, debt treatment on closing, ownership percentages, covenant definitions, rollover size.
## Calculations

None performed in this module. Numbers are quoted from cited sources or referenced to the CP-1 handoff. Implied equity value of the merger is Not calculable from the sources: the number of shares eligible for the $31.00 consideration, rollover shares and cashed-out equity awards are not disclosed in the pages read.

- Merger financing, buyer capital structure, rollover share count, treatment of existing notes and credit facilities, any change-of-control put: Not supplied. - Pages of the 10-K properties list and risk factors not read in full; no image or chart inspected.

The synthesis rests on the CP-1 financial handoff, the CP-1A business and transaction handoff and the CP-0 readiness handoff, checked against the filed sources below. Cutoff 2026-11-05; latest evidence is the Q3 10-Q and Q3 earnings release of October 27, 2026. This module gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion; relative value belongs to CP-3 and the committee's action bias to CP-6.

Upstream status carried: CP-0 and CP-1 and CP-1A each concluded with limitations. The CP-1A readiness judgment for CP-2 is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, not READY, so confidence below is not High. Category tags: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation, Insufficient Information.
## Findings
### Credit view

Assessment (Analyst Interpretation, confidence Medium). Caesars is a large, diversified US casino operator whose operating earnings are stable to slightly lower, whose financial risk is driven by leverage and a heavy fixed rent burden that sits outside its reported Adjusted EBITDA, and whose credit profile is currently dominated by an unresolved ownership change. The company covers its cash debt service and fixed rent from operating cash flow with a modest surplus, has reduced debt over 2026 and holds ample revolver liquidity, but net losses, thin fixed-charge coverage on a rent-inclusive basis and a refinancing concentration in 2029 and 2030 leave limited tolerance for an earnings shock or a more leveraged post-merger structure.

Basis: CP-1 table and calculations (LTM Adjusted EBITDA 3,573; face debt 11,659; net debt 10,795; rent-inclusive coverage 1.69x on the CP-1 calculation) and the CP-1A business, transaction and governance rows.

Thesis (Analyst Interpretation): stable multi-market gaming cash flow and good near-term liquidity support the credit, while rent-inclusive leverage near five times, concentrated 2029 and 2030 maturities and an unresolved buyer financing plan keep the credit view contingent on the post-merger capital structure.
### Key findings

First, earnings scale and diversification are real but trending slightly down. Adjusted EBITDA for the latest twelve months to September 30, 2026 is 3,573 on the CP-1 calculation, compared with 3,624 for FY2025. In Q3 2026 revenue grew 2.5% while Adjusted EBITDA fell 2.1% to 865 and the reported margin slipped to 29.4% from 30.8% (10-Q Q3 p41). The mechanism is cost growth in labor, gaming taxes, property taxes and insurance captive costs outpacing revenue, and a softer Las Vegas segment where Adjusted EBITDA fell to 343 from 379 on fewer convention events and lower leisure visitation (10-Q Q3 p46). The implication is that coverage cushions are narrowing even as reported revenue grows. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the mechanism.

Second, leverage looks moderate on the company definition but is materially higher once rent is counted. Face debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 3.26x and net debt 3.02x (CP-1 calculations). Adjusted EBITDA excludes lease expense on the VICI and GLPI leases, which are accounted for as financing obligations of 13,188 on the balance sheet and cost 1,370 in cash over the latest twelve months (CP-1 calculation). After deducting that rent, face debt is 5.29x and net debt 4.90x of the remaining 2,203. The mechanism is that rent is a largely fixed claim on property cash flow that is paid ahead of debt holders in practice; the implication is that a revenue or margin shock transmits to debt service more sharply than the headline leverage suggests. Category: Analyst Interpretation on documented figures; these rent-adjusted ratios are not company or covenant measures.

Third, coverage is adequate for cash obligations but thin on a total fixed-charge basis. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest paid for debt 4.82x over the latest twelve months, but covers cash interest plus cash rent only 1.69x (CP-1 calculations). In the nine months of 2026 interest expense, net of 1,712 exceeded operating income of 1,470, and the company reports net losses in each period (FY2025 net loss attributable of 502; nine months 2026 of 283). Free cash flow after capex was 582 over the latest twelve months (491 after distributions to noncontrolling interests) on lower capex of 507 in the nine months versus 648. The implication is that debt reduction capacity depends on holding capex down and operating cash flow stable. Category: Documentary Fact for figures; Analyst Interpretation for conclusions. The comparison of interest expense to operating income is an interpretation of reported figures; CP-1 did not compute a ratio.

Fourth, liquidity is good in the near term and the maturity wall is further out. Total liquidity at September 30, 2026 was 2,947 including cash of 864 and net revolver capacity, with the CEI revolver undrawn against 160 drawn at year-end 2025 (Q3 release p2; 10-Q Q3 p15, p19). Scheduled principal is only 28 for the rest of 2026 and 114 in 2027, then 646 in 2028 (revolver and Term Loan A due January 31, 2028), 1,574 in 2029 and 3,962 in 2030 (10-Q Q3 p16). The mechanism is that near-term amortisation is covered many times by liquidity, but the revolver and Term Loan A maturity in 2028 and the 2029 and 2030 maturities require market access or a refinancing under an owner whose capital structure is not yet known. Category: Documentary Fact.

Fifth, the pending merger changes who the borrower's owner is, and the credit-relevant terms are undisclosed. Stockholders approved the merger with Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC on September 22, 2026 at a cash price of 31.00 per share, with a reverse termination fee of 450 and a termination fee of 200 (10-Q Q3 p7-9). The buyer's financing, the treatment of existing notes and facilities, any change-of-control provision and the rollover amount are not disclosed in the sources read, and the 10-Q lists "risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction" (10-Q Q3 p57). The mechanism is that new debt at or above Caesars, or a change-of-control trigger on existing instruments, could raise leverage or force refinancing; the implication is that the monitoring posture is event-driven until the financing plan is disclosed. Category: Documentary Fact for the terms, Insufficient Information for financing and debt treatment. Missing evidence is not treated as an adverse conclusion.

Sixth, covenant headroom cannot be stated. The CEI revolver and Term Loan A have a maximum net total leverage ratio of 6.50:1 and a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of 2.0:1, tested on definitions that are not supplied, and the company states compliance at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 p20-21). Insufficient Information: covenant EBITDA and fixed charge definitions are missing, so headroom is Not calculable and the company's compliance statement is the only evidence. The 2.0:1 fixed charge coverage level is not comparable to the 1.69x rent-inclusive figure above because the covenant definition is unknown.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Scale and geographic diversification across 54 properties in 20 jurisdictions with four distinct earnings segments (Las Vegas, Regional, Caesars Digital, Managed and Branded) reduce dependence on a single market (CP-1A; 10-Q Q3 p10); Documentary Fact. Resilient regional performance and a growing digital segment offset Las Vegas weakness in the quarter: Regional Adjusted EBITDA rose to 524 from 506 and Caesars Digital to 44 from 28 (Q3 release p1), though part of the Regional gain is acquired scope from Caesars Windsor; Documentary Fact. Liquidity is strong relative to near-term obligations at 2,947, with an undrawn 2,250 CEI revolver and 25 Caesars Virginia revolver (CP-1; 10-Q Q3 p19); Documentary Fact. Debt was reduced by 246 in face value and net debt by 223 over the nine months (CP-1 calculation), and share repurchases stopped in 2026 (10-Q Q3 p53); Documentary Fact. Cash interest paid for debt fell to 580 in the nine months from 652 (10-Q Q3 p5), helping cash conversion; Documentary Fact. A large share of debt is secured with a lien on substantially all assets and guarantees from material domestic subsidiaries, and the 2029 and 2032 unsecured notes rank equally with unsecured claims (10-Q Q3 p21); Documentary Fact on structure only, with no statement on recovery. Variable-rate borrowing is about half of debt and carries a weighted average rate of 6.12% (10-Q Q3 p54), which lowers fixed-rate refinancing pressure but exposes interest cost to Term SOFR, about 61 per 100 basis points on the 10-K sensitivity at December 31, 2025 (10-K p95); Documentary Fact.

Weaknesses. Heavy lease financing obligations of 13,188 and cash rent of 1,030 in the nine months of 2026 create a fixed-charge burden that Adjusted EBITDA excludes (CP-1); Documentary Fact. Persistent net losses (FY2025 502, nine months 2026 283 attributable) mean no earnings buffer for debt service beyond operating cash flow (CP-1 table); Documentary Fact. Las Vegas, the highest-margin segment, is weakening with fewer convention events, lower occupancy of 89.1% versus 91.6% in Q3 and compressed rates (10-Q Q3 p45-46); Documentary Fact. Margin pressure from labor, gaming taxes, property taxes and captive insurance costs, with Adjusted EBITDA down while revenue is up (10-Q Q3 p41-43); Documentary Fact. Maturity concentration in 2029 and 2030 and the 2028 revolver and Term Loan A maturity (10-Q Q3 p16); Documentary Fact. The ownership change brings an undisclosed capital structure and transaction costs of 12 in Q3 and 22 in the nine months (10-Q Q3 p10); Documentary Fact on costs, Insufficient Information on structure. Data Incident litigation from 2023 remains open with losses not estimable, though the company states no material impact so far (10-K p121); Documentary Fact, with the outcome Insufficient Information. The reliance on Adjusted EBITDA add-backs is another weakness: transaction costs and other, net was 64 in the nine months of 2026 and stock-based compensation 70 (Q3 release p6); Documentary Fact. No add-back bridge to covenant EBITDA is supplied; Insufficient Information.
### Key credit risks

1. Post-merger capital structure and change of control. Severity: Critical. Mechanic: buyer financing may add leverage at or above Caesars, and existing instruments may contain change-of-control provisions. Implication: refinancing, leverage tolerance and monitoring posture are unresolved until the financing is disclosed. Basis: CP-1A transaction summary and gaps; Insufficient Information on the terms.

2. Fixed rent burden and rent-adjusted leverage. Severity: Material. Mechanic: cash rent of 1,370 over the latest twelve months is paid before equity and acts like senior debt service; a decline in Adjusted EBITDA reduces the cushion over interest plus rent, which stands at 1.69x. Implication: limited tolerance for an earnings shock; debt service coverage depends on rent-inclusive cash flow. Basis: CP-1.

3. Las Vegas softness and margin compression. Severity: Material. Mechanic: lower convention and leisure demand and rising costs reduce Adjusted EBITDA while revenue grows elsewhere. Implication: leverage drifts upward even without new debt. Basis: CP-1A operating model rows and CP-1 Q3 figures.

4. Refinancing concentration in 2028 to 2030. Severity: Material. Mechanic: 646 due in 2028, 1,574 in 2029 and 3,962 in 2030 require market access under a new owner. Implication: refinancing risk is back-ended but large; liquidity of 2,947 mitigates the 2026 and 2027 period only. Basis: CP-1 maturity ladder.

5. Variable-rate exposure. Severity: Minor. Mechanic: about 5.8 billion of term loans reset with Term SOFR. Implication: interest cost rises with rates; the sensitivity is stated at 61 per 100 basis points at December 31, 2025. Basis: CP-1 and 10-K p95.
6. Regulatory and litigation. Severity: Minor. Mechanic: gaming approvals for the merger and open Data Incident claims. Implication: timing risk and cash cost; amounts not estimable. Basis: CP-1A.

7. Digital hold variance and promotion cost. Severity: Minor. Mechanic: sports betting and iGaming hold and promotional spending swing segment earnings, which fell in Q2 and rose in Q3 2026 (Q2 and Q3 releases). Implication: volatility in a segment that is a growing share of earnings. Basis: CP-1A.
### Gaps ledger

- Merger financing, buyer capital structure, rollover size and treatment of existing debt on closing. Severity: Critical. Affects the capital-structure view, refinancing risk and covenant outlook. Action: obtain the Merger Agreement, Form 8-K of May 28, 2026 and proxy statement dated August 26, 2026.
- Covenant definitions, covenant EBITDA bridge and headroom. Severity: Material. Affects the view on default risk. Action: obtain the credit agreement and indentures. Not calculable until then.

- VICI and GLPI lease terms beyond the 10-K summary, including cross-default and rent-coverage tests other than the GLPI minimum adjusted revenue to rent ratio of 1.20:1. Severity: Material. Action: obtain lease documents.
- Ownership percentages and control rights. Severity: Minor to Material. Action: obtain the proxy statement.
- Discrete quarter cash flow (Q3 2026 operating cash flow, capex, cash interest). Severity: Minor. Action: derive from Q2 year-to-date data if needed; not supplied.
- Quantified management guidance. Severity: Minor. None is quantified in the releases; the Q1 CFO comment is qualitative Management Language.
- Acquirer name inconsistency (Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC versus Fertitta Entertainment, Inc.). Severity: Minor. Action: resolve from the merger agreement.
## Calculations

No new calculation is performed in this module. All figures are quoted from the CP-1 handoff's table and calculations or from the cited source pages. The statement that rent-inclusive leverage is "near five times" restates the CP-1 figures (5.29x on face debt, 4.90x on net debt) and is not a new ratio. One interpretive comparison, nine-month interest expense, net of 1,712 against nine-month operating income of 1,470, uses figures already reported in the 10-Q and is stated qualitatively, without a derived ratio. Recovery value is Not calculable and not assessed.
## Gaps

Listed in the gaps ledger above. The most important limits on this synthesis are the undisclosed merger financing and debt treatment, the missing covenant definitions and lease documents, and the use of derived LTM figures (Q4 2025 implied from FY2025 less nine months 2025) from CP-1. Confidence is Medium, not High, because the CP-1A readiness judgment for this module was READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and the Critical transaction gap is open.
## Next module

CP-5 should use the transaction facts, the open financing and change-of-control gaps, the end-date and fee mechanics and the unresolved acquirer-name distinction. Any module that goes beyond this fundamental view (relative value, instrument selection, portfolio fit) belongs to later modules and is outside this synthesis.
